newsitem.title: UK: Chinese imports of soyoil seen at 100,000T a month.
newsitem.headline: Chinese imports of soyoil seen at 100,000T a month.

text.p: Reports that 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes of soyoil was on its way to China for second-half December delivery were seen as on the low side by European vegetable oil traders.
"China has been taking an average of 300,000 to 350,000 tonnes of soyoil every quarter over the past two years, which puts the monthly average at over 100,000 tonnes," said one trader.

Traders said they had reports of vessels fixed from Brazil and Argentina and the U.S./Gulf for November/December which indicate around 155,000 tonnes of soyoil is due to arrive in China in late-December/early-January.

"As far as we know there are seven vessels fixed from south America and five from the U.S/Gulf for November/December which puts the figure at around 155,000 to 160,000 tonnes of soyoil, about the norm," said another trader.
Traders said they expect imports to China to stay around the current level into the New Year with a slight drop ahead of the South American new crop harvest.

"We may see a drop off ahead of the south American new crop becoming available, because unless they are really desperate I can't see the Chinese paying a $20 premium for U.S. soyoil when South American material will soon be on the market," a trader said.
"China is already fixing vessels from Brazil and Argentina for May/Jun shipments," said another trader. --Jim Ballantyne, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8062
